` and `cmake --build --preset

# Trail #11 Plan — "Unit tests are failing in Debian on PC"

- Trail: #11
- Type: bug | Priority: high | Status: open | Phase: planning
- ACs: (1) `./build/release/bin/tiffImageTest` passes. (2) `./build/release/bin/tiffExporterTest` passes all test cases.

## 1. AC-to-change mapping

| AC | Change that satisfies it |
|----|--------------------------|
| AC1 — `tiffImageTest` passes | Fixtures are present and real when git-lfs is available: `build.sh` now runs `git submodule update --init --recursive` and `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull` before configure, so the 2 file-dependent cases (`fax2d.tif`, `jim___ah.tif`, `cramps-tile.tif`) get real TIFFs. On machines without git-lfs, the new configure-time check in `tests/CMakeLists.txt` fails fast with actionable setup instructions instead of the cryptic `Invalid byte order in TIFF header` exception — making the AC achievable by following the printed remedy. The 2 synthetic-stream cases are unaffected. |
| AC2 — `tiffExporterTest` passes all test cases | Same fixture fix: all 6 TEST_CASEs read LFS-backed fixtures, so resolving the submodule fixtures via `build.sh` (or manually per README) restores real TIFFs and all 6 pass. The CMake sanity check guarantees a pointer checkout can no longer silently produce runtime failures; it stops the build at configure with a clear error. |

On machines where fixtures are already real (e.g. this machine), both ACs
already pass; the changes keep them green and make the failing Debian setup
actionable. No library, test-source, or CI changes.

## 2. Ordered change list

1. **`tests/CMakeLists.txt`** — add a configure-time fixture sanity check:
   - `file(GLOB ...)` for `*.tif`, `*.tiff`, `*.tif2` under
     `tests/libtiff-pics`. If zero matches →
     `FATAL_ERROR "test fixtures missing; run: git submodule update --init --recursive"`.
   - For each match: `file(READ <f> FIRST_BYTES LIMIT 4 HEX)`; if the result is
     not `49492a00` ("II*") nor `4d4d002a` ("MM*"), collect the offender.
   - If any offender was collected → `FATAL_ERROR` with actionable instructions:
     install git-lfs (Debian package name `git-lfs`), then
     `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then
     `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`.
   - Placement: near the top of the tests CMakeLists, before/independently of
     target definitions; enforcement point for the whole build.
2. **`build.sh`** — before configure:
   - Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`.
   - If git-lfs is available (`git lfs version` succeeds), run
     `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`.
   - Otherwise print a warning on stderr that fixtures may be unresolved LFS
     pointers and tests will fail (the new CMake check enforces it). Do NOT
     hard-fail — keep `build.sh` usable; CMake check is the enforcement point.
   - Leave `build.bat` unchanged; the README covers Windows setup.
3. **`README.md`** — add a concise "Building from source / Running the tests"
   section:
   - Prerequisites: CMake >= 3.22, C++20 compiler, git, git-lfs.
   - Clone with submodules (`git clone --recursive ...`).
   - `git lfs pull` / the `build.sh` handles it.
   - Build via `./build.sh [preset]`.
   - Run tests via `ctest --preset gcc-linux-release --output-on-failure`.

     LFS; a missing git-lfs checkout fails tests with the new clear configure
     error.
   - Manual remedy commands (install git-lfs, `git submodule update --init
     --recursive`, `git -C tests/libtiff-pics lfs pull`).

     LFS fixtures in `tests/libtiff-pics` and fails with setup instructions
     instead of "Invalid byte order in TIFF header".
   - `### Added` bullet for the README build/test instructions.
   - (Fold both into the changelog section appropriately if cleaner.)

   `include/tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp`), test sources, CI workflow
   (`.github/workflows/workflow.yml`), `reference_images`, the submodule
   pointer, or the submodule "modified content" noise.
